svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Figure 1. Choosing a browser from what the task requires
svg.desc: Four questions asked in order. First, does the engagement require attributable traffic, in which case use a normal identifiable browser. Second, must a target be unable to tell your session from anyone else's, in which case use Tor Browser unmodified. Third, must your sessions be unlinkable to each other, in which case use a separate profile or machine per identity. Otherwise use any browser with a content blocker and accept the tracking.
svg.text: Figure 1: Ask What the Task Requires, Not How Private You Want To Be
Work down the list. Stop at the first question you answer yes to. Most professional work stops at question 3.
QUESTION 1
Does the scope agreement or the program
policy require attributable traffic?
A registered source address, an identifying header
YES
Use an ordinary, identifiable browser and profile
Register your source address if you were asked to. Add the header if one is specified.
Nothing else in this lesson applies, and applying it anyway is a scope violation that can
remove you from the program. Lesson 1.1 warned about exactly this.
QUESTION 2
Must a target be unable to tell your session
apart from anybody else's?
This is unattributability
YES
Tor Browser, unmodified
Uniformity is the only strategy that delivers this, and it only works while you are identical
to every other user. Change nothing. Set the security level the task needs, and accept the
speed, the challenges and the breakage as the price.
QUESTION 3
Must your sessions be impossible to link
to each other, or to your other identities?
This is unlinkability
YES
A separate profile or machine for each identity
Separation does the work. A randomising browser inside each one adds to it. A configured
Firefox works equally well. What matters is that the identities never share a profile.
Most professional security work stops here.
OTHERWISE
No answer above was yes.
Personal browsing, reading, shopping
Any browser you like, with a content blocker
Accept the tracking, and keep this browser strictly out of the other layers. A tool you find
unpleasant will be abandoned, and an abandoned control protects nothing.
The common error is to answer question 2 when the task only asked question 3.
Unattributability costs a great deal and is rarely what the work needs. Unlinkability costs very little and is usually the real requirement.
